title: Review in rounds, each with a new lens
statement: Review in rounds, each through a new lens and again after every change, fixes and display code included, and stop only after two rounds in a row find nothing new.
example: On one set of nine lessons, successive rounds found 5, 5, 5, 1 and 1 critical faults before a round found none.
detail: One course's review loop changed its lens each round; its lenses included a walk as a student who gets everything right and one who gets every gated item wrong twice, a line-by-line check against the source lessons, a simulated first read by someone outside the project, and a comparison with a course already shipped. On the same nine lessons the first five rounds found 5, 5, 5, 1 and 1 critical faults, and the sixth, run on what had changed, found none (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19-R2.md` and the later rounds beside it). After the content had converged, 8 new engine commits brought a round that found two critical faults, and the loop's rule then sent the fix commit itself to fresh eyes; an earlier round had found a fix that solved its target while breaking a field it didn't need to touch.
against: Re-review is scoped to what changed: by the loop's rule, "a lens never runs twice on unchanged content" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-20-R6.md`, lines 9-10).
